issues.detail: Lines 335-342 of the tex contain a labelled result, 'Proposition (The E-step is exact) \label{prop:em-estep}: Since the posterior factor graph is a tree, one forward and one backward sum--product sweep return the exact single-site and pairwise posterior marginals ... the E-step requires neither a variational approximation nor Monte Carlo sampling'. It sits squarely inside the audited range (lines 1-600) and is a mathematical assertion, not prose colour -- and it is the load-bearing justification for the whole E-step. It appears nowhere in Ch08a.json: it is not proved, not skipped, not even listed. Every other numbered environment in the range has an entry (including the purely pictorial arrow diagram, honestly recorded as 'skipped'), so its silent absence reads as coverage where there is none. Note also that the Lean model is the *finite/grid* latent space, in which exactness of sum-product on a tree is a real theorem that was not attempted.

issues.detail: Item status is honestly 'defined', but its note claims a proof: 'the variance-matching claim implicit in Var(eps)=1-alpha^2 is proved (alpha^2*1+(1-alpha^2)=1), i.e. the chain is stationary with unit variance.' The Lean content is 'theorem ch08a_em_chain (alpha : R) : alpha ^ 2 * 1 + (1 - alpha ^ 2) = 1 := by ring'. That is an arithmetic tautology over the reals: no random variable, no variance operator, no reference to ch08a_em_chain_next, and no use of independence of eps_i from a_{i-1} (which is exactly the modelling hypothesis that makes Var(a_i) = alpha^2 Var(a_{i-1}) + Var(eps_i) true in the first place). The tex claim at lines 23-31 -- a_1 ~ N(0,1), a_i = alpha a_{i-1} + eps_i with Var(eps)=1-alpha^2, hence stationary unit variance -- is therefore not verified; only the numerical bookkeeping is. The gloss 'i.e. the chain is stationary with unit variance' overstates what 'ring' established.
issues.suggested_status: defined (with the note weakened to 'arithmetic consistency of the variance budget only')

issues.detail: Three items carry status 'proved' for statements that hold by 'rfl' against the auditor's own definitions, so nothing about the thesis's objects is tested. (i) noname-5, tex 194-198, 'p_theta(a,c|x) = p_theta(a,c,x)/p_theta(x)': Lean 'theorem ch08a_bayes ... : ch08a_post P z = P z / ch08a_marg P := rfl', where ch08a_post is *defined* as that ratio -- Bayes' rule cannot fail here by construction. (ii) eq:em-marginalisation, tex 122-129: 'ch08a_marg P = sum z, P z := rfl', again the definition; only the companion ch08a_em_marginalisation_pair (sum over pairs = sum_c sum_a) has content. (iii) eq:em-log-mixture, tex 365-378: 'Real.log (ch08a_em_mixture_kernel ...) = Real.log (sum c, p c * ch08a_gauss ...) := rfl', pure unfolding. Each JSON note does disclose the rfl, so this is a labelling rather than a substantive problem -- but a reader scanning the 'status' column counts three more verified displays than exist. Recommend a distinct status word (e.g. 'definitional') for rfl-only entries.
